analysis.title: Duttenhoefer's Daily 05.11.2026
key_insights: S&P 500 rose 158bps to 7688 (+12.3% ytd) on the 'blue wave'. Thematic spreads show less data center and defense budget exposure against more subsidies and homebuilding. Semis kept falling, Amazon rose 6%, MSFT hit a new all-time high.

21 of GS's US baskets had a >3 sigma move the previous day, the 2nd highest on a 1-year lookback (June 5 was 25). Market focus is 'less data center, less defense budget, more homebuilding and more healthcare subsidies'.
Basket moves: ACA Beneficiaries +9%, Homebuilders +7%, Hyperscalers +4%, versus NeoClouds -8%, Power Up -6%, Defense Spending -5%.

Cross-asset moves: US 10yr fell to 4.85%, Brent at $95 (-20% in 4 days on Iran deal hopes), Gold $4117 (-5% ytd), Bitcoin $80k (-8% ytd). Kospi fell 6%, driven by SK Hynix -10% and Samsung -8%. US NFPs are due tomorrow.

Positioning: October is the most significant month for mutual fund fiscal year ends (tax losses), which set up the midterms as a clean positioning clearing event. The desk says the most critical potential clearing event this year may still be ahead and is tied to equity capital markets.
Apple is cutting the daily amount its engineering teams can spend on AI from $300 to $200, with more cuts in the works and some allowances falling to $100 a day.
Uber said only 4 rides were ordered through an AI agent in its busiest October week (Halloween). More people used an AI agent to order food, but volume was still small.

Uber management said fuel cost impacts have been felt globally because of the Middle East war. It says it faces supply constraints rather than demand constraints, is investing in driver acquisition, retention and engagement, and saw early signs of supply improvement in October.

Peter (GS) on TMT moves: investor conversations focus on the magnitude of moves more than direction, and on when the market may over-price policy outcomes if moves continue (e.g. CSPs > Semis, drawdowns in IPPs or E&Cs, sharp rally in consumer discretionary).

China CIO tour in Beijing: expectations of large stimulus remain low, with YTD GDP growth inside the 4.5-5% target. Locals expect more domestic demand-side policy, focused on investment, if exports slow meaningfully next year. A stable US-China relationship is expected near term, with leader meetings at APEC (Nov 18-19) and the G20 (Dec 14-15).
GS raised STOXX-600 EPS growth forecasts to 18%/7% in 2026/27 from 15%/5%, on Financials and Commodities. Financials are over 30% of EURO STOXX earnings but only 10% of Euro Area economic activity.
G10 consumers benefit from healthy balance sheets and labor markets, but real income growth remains soft in most developed markets.
AI adoption among US establishments rose 0.8% to 24.6%, expected to reach 28.6% in the next 6 months, and is approaching 50% in information, professional and finance sectors.

Stat of the Day: since 1952 the 12 months after a midterm election have been the S&P 500's strongest stretch of the four-year cycle. Across 18 midterms the index averaged +7.5% through year end, +13.9% over the next 6 months and +15.5% over 12 months, and was higher at both the 6 and 12 month marks in all 18 instances.

sector_views.rationale: STOXX-600 EPS growth forecasts raised to 18%/7% for 2026/27 on Financials and Commodities contributions.
GS baskets moved sharply higher (+7% and +9%) as markets priced more homebuilding and healthcare subsidies.
Baskets fell on the market theme of less data center and less defense budget (NeoClouds -8%, Power Up -6%, Defense Spending -5%).

earnings_insights: Uber (3Q call, reported in the week before 5 Nov 2026): management said it faces supply constraints rather than demand constraints and is making targeted driver supply investments, with early supply improvement seen in October. No EPS or revenue figures are given.
Apple: cutting daily engineering AI spend allowances from $300 to $200 per day, with more cuts planned. This is a reported company action, not an earnings figure.
GS TMT head Eric Sheridan discussed 3Q earnings takeaways, sector debates and preferred stock ideas in a 27-minute audio piece.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Yield fell on the day as equities rallied.
Decline attributed to Iran deal hopes.
Adoption by firms rose 0.8%, near 50% in information, professional and finance sectors.
Market attention is on the release tomorrow.

risk_factors: Over-pricing of policy outcomes if the sharp thematic moves continue (CSPs > Semis, IPPs and E&Cs drawdowns, consumer discretionary rally).
A clearing event tied to equity capital markets may still be ahead.
Middle East war and fuel costs, per Uber's call.
Weaker China exports could lead to domestic demand policy shifts, though large stimulus is not expected.
Real income growth remains soft in most developed markets.
vol_and_positioning: 21 of GS's US baskets had a >3 sigma move the previous day, the 2nd highest on a 1-year lookback (June 5 was 25).
October fiscal year ends for mutual funds (tax losses) made the midterms a clean clearing event for positioning.
GS sees the most critical potential clearing event for the market this year as possibly still ahead, tied to equity capital markets.
Investors focus on the magnitude of moves and on possible over-pricing of policy outcomes if moves continue.
geopolitical: Iran deal hopes drove Brent down 20% in 4 days.
Escalation and war in the Middle East raised fuel costs globally, per Uber's call.
Stable US-China relations expected near term, with leader meetings at APEC (Nov 18-19) and the G20 summit (Dec 14-15).
US midterm election outcome described as a 'blue wave', driving thematic moves in healthcare, homebuilding, data center and defense baskets.
